Good morning. You asked me for both sides of the private label plan, so here they are. The case for it is margin. Our own brands make about eight points more margin than the national brands, whereas the price for the customer is around twenty percent lower. That is a good deal for both sides. However, there are two problems. The first is cannibalization. Although the private label grows, part of that growth comes from our own national brands, not from the competitors. The second is the suppliers. Despite our good relationship, two big suppliers have already said that they will reduce their promotions with us if we give their space to our own brands. I concede that this is a real risk. But on balance, I would still move forward, slowly, in three categories first, with a clear review after six months.

In a visa interview, the officer may push back on your reason for the trip. A common version is this: you can take an online course from Brazil, so why do you need to travel? Do not get defensive, and do not argue. The best answer has two parts. First, concede the point. Yes, online courses exist, and some of them are good. Then give the counterargument in one short sentence: although the content is online, the case discussions happen in the classroom, with executives from other countries. That is the part you cannot download. Notice the order. You start with what is true in the officer's argument, and only then do you say why your choice is still right. It sounds calm, it sounds honest, and it shows that you have thought about the question before.
First, she states the question in one sentence. Then she gives the bull case. After that, she gives the bear case. Next, she adds a caveat about her own data. Finally, she gives her view on balance.
